SCOUT INDEPENDENT README REVIEW of 02233e6: ACCEPT; no correctness blocker. I used the reader-first README rubric after rereading vision/mission and verified the new claims against current source/build. Confirmed: 17 aggregated modules exactly; 15 portable cross-projects plus two JVM-only projects; hashed n-gram and TF-IDF baselines exist; grakern pin is exactly 0329c43 and the pinned checkout has no remote, while GitHub ls-remote reports repository not found; non-Public receipt identities require a key and fail closed; RemotePolicy rejects Raw and accepts only detector-certified PseudonymizedText; wholeWordTable is the sole public detector factory; view exports private-constructed CodexFlow/NarrativeScene; all five links exist; current main has no README delta since the candidate base; diff --check clean. The example is public API and the author supplied executable proof.

Reader nits, not landing blockers: (1) first code begins after 249 words; moving Smallest example above What it does would better satisfy Promise→Proof→Scope without changing content. (2) The quickstart proves the atlas rather than the central story↔recall mapping, but that is currently the smallest honest ordinary workflow because automatic construction does not exist; the adjacent hand-modeled-fixture sentence makes that boundary visible. (3) On a later README pass, say WOG is hand-authored in narrative types / plain-language expectations, never hand-authored AMR, to mirror the fixture contract and remove any ambiguity in hand-modeled. The candidate materially improves accuracy and does not overclaim release, providers, calibration, visualization publication, or remote state.
